Carries every remaining item from the /ship-it critical review of ancora-yzu (2026-09-03), plus the follow-ups the ship itself exposed. Split out at delivery so ancora-yzu could close on its merge; nothing here blocked the 1.0 merge.

Source of record: /Users/mz/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-03/ancora-yzu-spec-anchored-successor/20260903-052243-consolidated.md (review_commit 5220686). Nine personas, 100 raw findings to 81 unique to 66 calibrated after a skeptic pass, 42 severity adjustments, 25 consensus, ZERO critical.

Three of the 58 fix-now items are already done: F1 (ancora.review contract pass) and F2/F3 (test isolation races) were the two ship blockers, fixed as ancora-ayj and ancora-rdx and merged in 5d9cb400. F20 (collapse the four mix-subprocess helpers) was folded into ancora-rdx and is also done.

Children group the remaining findings by the seam they touch rather than one ticket per finding, so each child is a coherent unit of work. Every child enumerates its constituent F-numbers with file:line so no finding is lost. The 15 findings the review DROPPED are deliberately not carried; their reasons are in the report and should not be relitigated.

NOT CARRIED — the 15 findings the review dropped in its skeptic pass. Reasons are in the report; do not relitigate. In brief: the no-op --debug flag, parallelising the three serial parse phases (measured 330ms, changes which parse error wins), the acknowledged-subject full comparison, the seven inert Prism grammars, an assertion-message style sweep, the two parallel git-fixture helpers, three untestable-as-written clauses, a print stylesheet nobody needs, three return shapes on the front door, spec.next lacking --root, the eleven-parameter all_findings, resolver bare maps wanting a struct, Module.concat minting atoms, two unused Severity exports, and cosmetic two-branch conds.

Sequencing worth respecting: xla.9 (ETS memo decision) gates part of xla.3, and ancora-gqb needs its contract line before F17 in xla.9 becomes testable. xla.1 and xla.2 are the two with concrete crash paths and are the natural first wave.

Review bar: these are tracked rather than fixed-in-place because the branch they would have landed on is merged and gone — ancora 1.0 shipped as 5d9cb400. Review-bar-override: post-ship follow-ups on a closed epic; there is no open branch to fix them on.

It was already IMPLEMENTED by codex run p47-impl-1 in stage worktree /Users/mz/src/ancora-p47-libpaths (branch ancora-p47/uncovered-lib-paths, 53036d7, one commit on 5d9cb40). Re-checked today: compile, format, 333 tests, spec.check all green. Orchestrator: resume from IMPLEMENTED, do not respawn an implementer.

Seven tickets carry a "Ruling needed" block and will park for Manuel unless a ruling comment is on the ticket first: n24, u38, v1n, 11w, sfu, xla.5, xla.9. Each block names the ticket's own recommended default.

Merge-conflict hot spots to expect (rebase worker territory, not real conflicts): lib/ancora/gate.ex is touched by xla.1, xla.2, xla.3, xla.6, and p47; lib/ancora/output.ex by xla.2, xla.5, xla.6; .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md by xla.2, xla.6, xla.7, 11w, sfu, u38. Merge batching is on.

Stale text left in place, corrected by status notes on the tickets: p47 and sfu say trunk is red (main CI has been green since the 13:17 workflow_dispatch run once the default branch moved to main); n24 says it is not an epic child (it is now).

RULINGS COMPLETE (Manuel, 2026-09-03). Every decision ticket now carries a RULING comment; workers should not park for these.
- ancora-v1n: append-only authorization requires the requirement id in affects:.
- ancora-n24: retires: field on the ADR; a subject id covers its requirements.
- ancora-sfu: acknowledgments promoted to config.yml severities/overrides; trailer is a dev convenience; loud warning when trailer-only.

- ancora-xla.9: F9 DELETE the memo (narrow the must under an ADR); F13 deprecate spec-exceptions, remove in 2.0; F17 moved to ancora-gqb.
- ancora-gqb: writes the watched-card contract line and swaps the regex extractor for the AST resolver in the same diff.
- ancora-xla.5: versioned superset JSON payload; public API is the two parse_file/2 functions plus Ancora.check/2 and Ancora.validate/2.
- ancora-u38: DEFERRED OUT OF THIS EPIC (parent cleared, revisit 2026-10-01). Ancora carries no cache unless a post-xla.3 Atlas bench forces the question. Fifteen children remain.

DAG after rulings: gqb, xla.9, and xla.3 are all ready now. Remaining edges: xla.3 blocks u38 (outside the epic), p47 blocks sfu, xla.2 blocks 11w, v1n blocks n24. Governing principle for graders: ancora exists to carry less machinery than specled_ex. Prefer deletion and plain function arguments over any memo, registry, or cache.

SCOPE NOTE (2026-09-03): standalone ticket ancora-8t2 closed as superseded; its surviving fix (push-to-main base via github.event.before in ci.yml) is now F30b inside ancora-xla.5. No new child, no new edge. ci.yml is touched by xla.5 only.

PHASE 0 STOP — epic-wide gate red before any worker spawned (2026-09-03, orchestrate-epic).

Preflight passed, epic admitted (15 task children, not a portfolio), worktree /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla entered at 5d9cb40, epic started with phase:implementing, merge batching on, laborer codex/remembers has headroom. Known-red baselines resolve to none: the repo has no CLAUDE.md, so nothing is waivable.

The stop: the epic worktree smoke is RED on an unmodified base. 331 tests, 7 failures, 210s wall clock against a 32s baseline. Every failure is ExUnit.TimeoutError at 60000ms inside Ancora.TestCase.run_mix_subprocess, in File.cp_r! or the port read. A failed-only re-run reproduced 4 of 7, so these are not single-sample flakes and are not flake-acceptable under the same-seed protocol.

Attribution: this is ancora-s1o exactly, and not a regression from anything in this epic. Three of the failing tests are the ones s1o names by name. The base commit is main's tip with zero changes on top. test/support/ancora_case.exs copies the whole build path on every subprocess call, about 30 calls per run, and _build in this worktree is 48 MB. Running test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs alone passes but takes 28 seconds for one test, which is the copy cost with nothing else competing.

Second, independent factor: host load average was 162 on 10 cores, with 161 beam processes, three other Claude sessions, and a VM at 185 percent CPU. Memory was fine at 41 percent free, so the admission load brake did not fire on its own terms. Contention amplified the defect; it did not create it.

Why this stops the whole epic rather than one child: every child's final tier and every merge gate runs this suite. Fifteen children against a suite that fails one run in three produces false reds that get misattributed to tickets, burned bounce attempts, and a flake-accept ceiling blown early.

No implementer was spawned. ancora-p47 stays at IMPLEMENTED, unverified, in /Users/mz/src/ancora-p47-libpaths. Nothing is lost by resuming later.

Recommendation put to Manuel: pull ancora-s1o into this epic as the first child, blocking every other child. Its own description already said it was meant to ride this fast-follow wave. It has been given Verification, Allowed touches, Out of Scope, and Merge gate sections and its literal backslash-n corruption is fixed, so it is admittable the moment the scope call is made.

Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5.jsonl

Epic paused at Phase 0 on an epic-wide red gate, before any worker was spawned. Full evidence is in the PHASE 0 STOP comment above. Console seeded and published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/8cc34715-5fb4-4d95-8599-ed924e6acec5 and recorded on the description.

Resolution required from Manuel: one scope decision, either pull ancora-s1o into this epic as the first child blocking the other fifteen, or authorize orchestrating against a suite that fails about one run in three.

Counters at pause: console_triggers=1 console_redeploys=1.

RUN STATE after the s1o collision (orchestrate-epic, 2026-09-03 17:53). The epic is idle by choice, waiting on an external merge. No park, no escalation, nothing needed from Manuel right now.

Sequence: Manuel approved pulling ancora-s1o in as the epic's prerequisite. I re-parented it, wired it to block the twelve otherwise-unblocked children, created its stage worktree, and spawned a Codex implementer at 17:48. The ancora 1.0 ship session had already implemented the same ticket and posted IMPLEMENTED at 17:44. I killed my worker at 17:51, removed the stage worktree and branch, and discarded its one commit.

My mistake, recorded so the next run does not repeat it: I read the ticket, then spent about thirteen minutes on worktree setup, rigor and boundary checks, and prompt rendering, then spawned without re-reading. Ticket admission step 9 puts the start immediately before the spawn precisely so state gets re-checked there. A single bw-marker latest call at that moment would have returned IMPLEMENTED and stopped the spawn. Adding to LESSONS.

Both ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 are ceded to the ship session's PR against main and remain children of this epic, in_progress, not driven from here. The suite fix is 35372ed, read and judged sound independently, with ten consecutive green full-suite runs reported at 31 to 59 seconds against the 210 seconds this epic measured.

The other fourteen children stay blocked behind ancora-s1o, which is the correct state: the epic worktree /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla sits at 5d9cb40, and every child records that as its admission base. When the ship PR merges, the work is to rebase the epic branch onto the new main, update the Base: line and the recorded base in each child, close ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 against the merge, and admit the first real wave. Building on their unmerged branch instead would be fragile and is deliberately not being done.

Counters: console_triggers=3 console_redeploys=2, one redeploy owed and being published now.

LESSONS
- [other] A cost a grader calls affordable must be measured under repetition, not at one sample. The per-call build copy was reviewed, priced at one sample, waved through, and then failed the suite about one run in three. (from ancora-s1o)
- [other] Re-read the ticket marker in the same breath as the spawn, not at the top of admission. Minutes of setup sit between them and another session can finish the ticket in that window. (from ancora-s1o)

CORRECTION to the rebase plan in my previous comment (2026-09-03 18:02). I wrote that the post-merge work includes updating the recorded base in each child. That is wrong and would do damage if followed literally.

Checked all fourteen remaining children. None carries a literal base sha as its admission base; every Verification and Merge gate section says 'the epic base sha recorded at admission' as a phrase, which is deliberate and stays correct across a rebase. Only three occurrences of the literal 5d9cb40 exist anywhere in the children, and all three are historical narrative about the 1.0 squash merge rather than an admission base:
- ancora-sfu twice, describing how the squash destroyed two Spec-Ack trailers and produced the 31 change/uncovered_file warnings, and a status note about the stale trunk-is-red framing.
- ancora-xla.5 once, in F30b, citing that spec.check --base 5d9cb40 passes because that is what github.event.before would have been for the post-merge push.

Rewriting any of those to a new sha would break the account they give. Leave them.

So the post-merge work is smaller than I said: rebase /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla onto the new main, update only the epic description's Base: line, close ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 against the merge sha, and admit the first wave. No per-child edits.
